dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before writing any code, the agent read the entire RFC linearly in ~200-line chunks (sed -n through lines 1-2800), checked total length with wc -l, and examined hex dumps of test files. Genuine upfront orientation, above a mere skim.
Deliberately grepped for section '4.1.1', '4.1' and 'Appendix' to locate FSE table construction and the predefined-distribution tables before implementing — targeted section-hunting, not pure recall.

Repeatedly rediscovered the Frame_Content_Size field-size mapping (fcsF=2 => 4 bytes, not 2) through empirical hex-dump debugging of test artifacts across many steps, rather than having extracted this explicit RFC field layout correctly on the first pass. Indicates weak internalization of a plainly-stated layout.

Got treeless (lt=3) vs compressed (lt=2) literals handling backwards ('My code has this backwards'), another field-semantics detail available directly in the text but reverse-engineered from observed failures.

Backward bitstream initialization (bsRef/bsInit conditions) was misread repeatedly and fixed by trial-and-error and hex inspection; agent admits 'I've been stuck on this for too long,' showing the mental model of the bit-level format was never made precise.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent invested real upfront effort reading the whole RFC and hunting the FSE/appendix sections before coding (above the level-3 skim), but its actual internalization of bit-level details was shallow: several explicitly-specified field layouts (FCS size mapping, treeless-literals semantics, backward-bitstream init) were implemented wrong and then reverse-engineered empirically from hex dumps of test files rather than re-derived carefully from the text. This falls short of level 5's 'gets most field layouts right on the first careful pass' and well short of level 8's systematic extraction and spec-example cross-checking, landing at 4 — thorough reading effort undermined by weak comprehension and observation-driven correction.

dimensions.name: Staged build of decoder components

evidence.note: Agent explicitly decides to 'write the complete zstd_decompress.c implementation in one comprehensive file' and does so before running anything — the monolithic approach that matches the low anchor, not a staged milestone plan.

Emergent (not planned) recognition that raw blocks work (simple, img.png) while compressed blocks fail — a loose implicit ordering rather than a deliberate simplest-to-hardest milestone sequence with pre-set done-checks.

Debugging is reactive and component-by-component (FCS parsing, then literals type handling, then bitstream), but each fix triggers a full-file rewrite rather than isolating and independently verifying a single milestone before building on it.

Repeated full rewrites of the whole decoder chasing bitstream bugs, with no localized milestone that had been proven-good to fall back on — confirming failures were not kept localized as the high anchors require.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's defining choice was to write the whole decoder at once before running (anchor 0 behavior), but the surrounding work shows loose implicit ordering — headers first, raw blocks recognized as working before compressed — and reactive per-component debugging, which lifts it above pure 0. It never established explicit ordered milestones or per-component completion criteria, and repeatedly rewrote the entire file rather than staging independently-verifiable components, so it falls squarely at the anchor-3 description: loose implicit ordering without explicit milestones.

dimensions.name: Differential testing against zstd -d

evidence.note: Attempted to obtain a reference via `which zstd && zstd -d ... -o /tmp/rep_expected` and md5sum it — the right differential instinct — but found zstd unavailable in the sealed env, so reference-based diffing was impossible.

Ran individual artifacts (img.png, audio.wav, video.mp4, repetitive) and compared output byte-size/md5 against known expected values to localize failures, concluding raw blocks work and compressed blocks fail — verification used to isolate the failing component.

Primary verification loop was repeatedly running test.sh (which bakes expected md5/size checks over the visible artifact set); no self-generated per-feature inputs (each FCS width, FSE mode, treeless, dictionary) were ever crafted or diffed.
Confirmed correctness by matching exact expected byte count (50529) and md5 for img.png rather than eyeballing — byte-level comparison, but only over the provided visible inputs.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond merely running test.sh (anchor 3): it tried to procure the reference decoder, and ran individual artifacts comparing size/md5 to expected values to localize raw-vs-compressed failures. But it never reached anchor 5's byte-for-byte comparison against `zstd -d` on inputs beyond test.sh — the reference was unavailable and it crafted no new feature-targeted inputs, confining all verification to the small visible artifact set. That places it at a 4, interpolating between the test.sh-only (3) and beyond-test.sh reference-diff (5) anchors.

dimensions.name: Tracking feature coverage across the horizon

evidence.note: After reading the RFC the agent wrote the whole decoder in one shot with no feature checklist or coverage map; 'Plan' lines are boilerplate ('Compile / Test'), not a running status of the many required features.

Only real progress metric is the visible test pass count ('2/6 tests pass'). This is crude test-result awareness, not a map of which spec features (dictionaries, multi-frame, FSE modes, skippable frames) are done vs pending.

Discovered the treeless literals variant (lt=3) only by accidentally encountering it while debugging, not from a tracked feature list — matches the level-3 'discovers missing features only by accident' anchor.
Repeated full rewrites re-fixing the same FCS-parsing and bitstream bugs; the agent circles on the same two components without a mechanism detecting the lack of progress.
Only at the very end does it note 'I've been stuck on this for too long' — late recognition of stalled debugging, and it still proposes more of the same rather than a structured re-diagnosis.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent had only a vague, test-count-based sense of progress and no explicit coverage map against the spec's feature list; it discovered a required feature (treeless) by accident and circled through ~10 full rewrites re-fixing the same FCS/bitstream bugs, recognizing the stall only at the final step. This matches the level-3 anchor ('vague recollection of progress; discovers missing features only by accident') and falls well short of level 5's maintained running feature list.

dimensions.name: Diagnosing and correcting bit-level bugs

evidence.note: Wrote debug programs (debug2-debug4) that dumped byte-level frame-header state and compared FCS/block-size against expected values, tracing the mismatch to a genuine root cause: the Frame_Content_Size field mapping (fcsF=2 means 4 bytes, not 2). Returned to the RFC to correct the model — classic level-8 isolation.

Repeatedly re-diagnosed and re-fixed the same fcsS mapping bug across multiple full rewrites and sed edits, indicating a shaky mental model and non-durable fixes rather than a single clean correction.

Formed specific stage-level hypotheses: treeless literals handling backwards (82), bsRef condition never triggering because p==e (89), bsInit using incremented pos instead of start (95-98). Good hypothesis formation about the responsible component.
Recurrent full-file rewrites to 'fix' bugs regressed proven code (duplicate declarations, sed corruption), the opposite of correcting without regressing working components.
Ends stuck — never converged on the FSE/backward-bitstream failure; compressed blocks never passed despite many cycles, so the harder root cause was never located.

dimensions.reasoning: For the frame-header/FCS bug the agent performed genuine level-8 work: dumping intermediate state via debug programs, comparing against expected values, and revising its RFC interpretation at the true root cause. But the overall arc is dragged down by repeated whole-file rewrites that regressed proven components, circling on the same bug across many cycles, and a failure to isolate the harder FSE/bitstream divergence — the opposite of the '8/10' 'without regressing proven components' standard. This blend of real root-cause tracing with non-durable, regression-prone execution places it at a 6, above the plain hypothesis-fix-retest of anchor 5 but well short of systematic, durable correction.

rubric.task_read: Build a from-scratch Zstandard decoder in C, reverse-engineering the entire wire format from RFC 8878 alone, with no reference to libzstd. This is a very long-horizon, high-complexity task: many interdependent sub-formats (frame headers, three block types, four literal encodings, FSE/Huffman entropy coding in four table modes, sequence machinery with repeat-offset history, dictionaries) that must all be bit-exact against `zstd -d`. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in spec-reading, staged milestone construction, and building verification/differential-testing infrastructure, because bugs are subtle bit-level errors that compound and are near-impossible to fix by barrelling ahead.

dimensions.name: Spec comprehension & format reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Reading and correctly internalizing RFC 8878's bit-level format details (endianness, FSE/Huffman construction, exact field layouts) before and while implementing each component.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The entire deliverable is a faithful implementation of one dense spec with no reference implementation to peek at; a single misread field (e.g. FSE state update order, offset code baseline, window-size formula) silently corrupts output. Getting the contract right from the text is the dominant source of difficulty.

anchors.0: Starts coding a decoder from prior memory of zstd without consulting the RFC; guesses at field layouts.
anchors.3: Skims the RFC for the frame header but implements FSE/Huffman/sequences from vague recall, returning to the text only when stuck.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant RFC sections before implementing each major component and gets most field layouts and formulas right on the first careful pass.
anchors.8: Systematically works section-by-section, extracting exact bit orderings, baseline/extra-bit tables, FSE normalization and state-init rules, and the treeless/dictionary edge cases directly from the text; notes ambiguities and resolves them against the spec's examples rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Builds a precise mental (or written) model of every sub-format including the subtle corners (LL=0 repeat-offset special case, overlapping match copies, predefined-table distributions, dictionary entropy/offset preloading), cross-checks interpretations against the RFC's worked examples and internal consistency, and revisits the text to disambiguate whenever an implementation detail is underdetermined — sustained across the whole build.

dimensions.name: Staged build of decoder components
dimensions.description: Breaking the decoder into an ordered hierarchy of independently-verifiable milestones (frame header → raw/RLE blocks → literals → FSE → Huffman → sequences → dictionaries) each with a done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The format has a natural dependency order; attacking it as one monolithic push guarantees a tangle of untestable code where the first bug is unlocatable. Sequencing from simplest decodable inputs to hardest is what makes progress observable.

anchors.0: No structure; attempts to write the whole decoder at once before running anything.
anchors.3: Loose implicit ordering (headers first) but no explicit milestones or per-component completion criteria.
anchors.5: Clear component-by-component plan following the natural dependency chain, implementing and roughly checking each before moving on.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones from simplest (raw block, then RLE) to hardest (compressed literals, sequences, dictionaries), each paired with a concrete way to confirm it works before building on it, so failures stay localized.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each stage is chosen to be independently testable against real inputs, sequenced to maximize early feedback, with the ordering revisited as complexity is discovered (e.g. deferring dictionary support until core entropy paths are proven), keeping the whole horizon under control.

dimensions.name: Differential testing against zstd -d
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — byte-diffing against the reference `zstd -d`, generating targeted inputs per feature, isolating failures — beyond the handful of visible test.sh cases.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grading set exercises every feature and demands byte-identical output; test.sh is explicitly insufficient. Without self-built differential tests over diverse inputs (each FCS width, each block/literal/FSE mode, dictionaries, checksums), bit-level bugs pass silently until grading.

anchors.0: Only runs the build; assumes correctness with no output comparison, or relies on eyeballing.
anchors.3: Runs test.sh and stops there, treating its pass as done.
anchors.5: Compares decoder output byte-for-byte against `zstd -d` on several inputs beyond test.sh, confirming a match.
anchors.8: Deliberately generates inputs that exercise specific features (each FCS width, RLE vs raw vs compressed blocks, 1- vs 4-stream literals, each FSE mode, checksummed and dictionary frames) and diffs each against the reference, using mismatches to localize the failing component.
anchors.10: Builds a systematic differential harness covering the full feature matrix (including corner cases like overlapping matches, treeless literals, multi-frame and skippable-frame inputs), crafts minimal reproducers to bisect bit-level discrepancies, and treats byte-identical parity across the whole matrix — not just test.sh — as the standing definition of done.

dimensions.name: Tracking feature coverage across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which of the many required features are done, in-progress, or untouched, and detecting when debugging has stalled or is circling.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec lists a long feature checklist and the build spans many sessions of effort; losing track means shipping with silent gaps (e.g. forgetting the treeless variant or LL=0 case) or thrashing on one bug while others remain unbuilt.

anchors.0: No sense of remaining work; jumps between features reactively, loses track of what's covered.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; discovers missing features only by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of required features and their status, checking off components as they verify.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, accurate coverage map against the spec's feature list, knows at any point what's proven vs pending, and notices when a debugging effort has stopped making progress rather than grinding indefinitely.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise done-vs-remaining picture across the entire horizon, recognizes circular/stuck debugging early and steps back to re-diagnose, and ensures no required feature (including the easily-forgotten edge cases) is silently skipped before declaring completion.

dimensions.name: Diagnosing and correcting bit-level bugs
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation or interpretation when output diverges from the reference — locating the true root cause rather than patching symptoms or barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Decoder bugs manifest as opaque byte mismatches far from their cause (a wrong FSE state transition corrupts everything downstream). Effective course-correction — re-reading the spec, forming hypotheses, isolating the faulty stage — is what converts a mismatch into a fix instead of a cascade of guesses.

anchors.0: On a mismatch, makes random tweaks or gives up; never revisits the assumption that caused it.
anchors.3: Patches surface symptoms (e.g. special-casing one input) without finding why output diverges.
anchors.5: When output differs, forms a plausible hypothesis about the responsible component and fixes it, re-testing afterward.
anchors.8: Systematically isolates the diverging stage (dumps intermediate state, compares against expected values from the spec), traces the mismatch to its root cause, and revises the interpretation — correcting the underlying misread rather than the symptom.
anchors.10: Treats each discrepancy as evidence, forms and tests competing hypotheses, returns to the RFC to correct a mistaken model when reality contradicts it, and generalizes the fix to related cases — consistently converting subtle bit-level failures into durable corrections without regressing proven components.
